surfaces.part: tiled roof (ridge, sloped tile courses, hipped ends)
white plaster wall with windows and timber frame (front face)
lower front: sliding doors, paper-screen window, engawa/veranda platform

answer.evidence: The main body is a farmhouse. Rows 11-34 are a large sloped tile roof with a ridge band at rows 13-16, stepped tile courses at rows 17-32 and a dark eave line and shadow at rows 33-34. The silhouette widens from 80 to 92 px across these rows, which is consistent with the roof slope and its overhanging eaves. Below it the front (south) face runs from about row 35 to row 75: plaster wall, timber posts, doors, screens and a veranda step. The veranda platform at rows 68-75 is drawn as a front face, but it is a minor detail. The roof reads as a top surface through criterion (c), and the front face is well over 3 rows, so the building reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a whole building (roof, plaster wall, timber lattice, shoji, stone footing), so it matches the reference kind. Measured facts support a pass: 14 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and 0% near-flat coverage, the same as both references. Shading shows about 5 steps on the blue-grey roof, with a ridge highlight and tile rows. The plaster is speckled, the wood has several browns, and the lattice and shoji panels add structure. The outline is mixed. Dark edges are 28% near-neutral, higher than the references' 7-9%, but most edges lean navy on the roof and brown on the wood, so they read as material tones. The roof is the weakest area: its rows are smoother than the references' scalloped tiles with per-tile highlights, and the palette is smaller (40 colours against 185 and 66). Overall it carries enough information not to look thinner or more sticker-like next to the references.

surfaces.part: tiled hip roof (sloped roof plane with tile rows, ridge at top, hip sides)
white plaster wall with window slits
timber lower facade with doors and paper-screen windows

answer.evidence: The building has a large sloped tiled roof covering rows 11-34, with horizontal tile courses, a ridge band at rows 13-16 and hip slopes at the sides. The roof ends in a dark eave line at rows 33-34 and overhangs the wall below, which fits evidence (c). Below it is a south front face of about 41 rows (rows 35-75): a plaster wall, timber posts, doors and screens, and a base. The roof is the main top surface and is clearly a foreshortened plane, not a front-facing strip.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a whole building with roof, plaster wall, lattice and door, so it matches the reference kind. Measured facts are at or above the references: 14 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 0% near-flat coverage like both references, and no 5x5 flat fills. The roof has a ridge highlight, tile rows and several blue-grey steps. The wall has plaster speckle, and the wooden lattice and door are shaded with grain. Dark edges are 28% near-neutral, higher than the references (7% and 9%), but most outline pixels lean toward blue-grey or brown beside the roof and wood. That makes the outline mixed rather than a uniform black sticker line. The roof tile scallops are less pronounced than the references' per-tile highlights, so the ramp is slightly shallower, but a careful artist would accept it beside the references.

surfaces.part: tiled roof (ridge cap and sloped tile courses, stepped eaves)
white plaster upper wall with lattice windows
wooden lower wall, sliding doors, paper-screen windows, and veranda/engawa porch

answer.evidence: The roof fills rows 11-34 as a large sloped plane. It has a ridge highlight at rows 12-16, tile courses at rows 19-32 that step outward, and a dark front-edge/eave line at rows 33-34. The silhouette widens from 80 to 92 px over those rows, which matches a hipped roof seen from above. Below it the south wall (rows 35-75) is a front face of well over 3 rows, with plaster, doors, and a porch. The roof is the main top surface, so the building reads as three_quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts are on par with the references: 14 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 0% near-flat coverage. Dark edge pixels are 28% neutral against 7-9% for the references, so the outline leans toward neutral and I call it mixed. By eye, the slate roof has roughly 4-5 steps (highlight ridge, light, mid, dark, deep eave) with only faint tile texture. The reference roofs have per-tile scallops with highlights and dark tile-shadow rows, so the candidate's roof reads smoother and more banded. The plaster wall has speckle, and the wooden lattice, shoji and door show several browns. The stone base is dark and has little per-stone shading, while the reference stone wall shades each stone. The candidate's outline is dark and fairly neutral around the roof and eaves, which gives some sticker feel next to the reference's tinted dark-material lines. Overall the candidate is competent and not flat, but it falls a little short of the references in roof texture and in the tint of its outlines. With only 40 distinct colours it is also less varied than the references' 66-185. Doubt goes to fail.
